name: containerize-aspnet-framework
description: Containerize specified ASP.NET (.NET Framework, not .NET Core) project for Windows Docker; make only changes required to run it. Unspecified settings use defaults. No infrastructure setup (assumed to be handled separately). No code changes beyond those required for containerization.

Settings: `.csproj`; Windows Server SKU (Core default or Full), version (2016/2019/2022); custom build/run images (default None); ports; container user (default `ContainerUser`); IIS; pre/post-build steps; GAC/MSI/COM; registry; environment; Windows roles/features; project-root files/directories and container targets; exclusions/`.dockerignore`; health-check URL/interval/timeout; other requirements/issues.

Procedure:
1. Review settings.
2. Create `progress.md` to track changes with check marks.
3. Determine .NET Framework version from `.csproj` `TargetFrameworkVersion`.
4. Select Windows Server image for detected version, SKU and Windows version. Tags: https://github.com/microsoft/dotnet-framework-docker/blob/main/README.aspnet.md#full-tag-listing
5. Required NuGet package: `Microsoft.Configuration.ConfigurationBuilders.Environment`. **DO NOT** install these if they are missing. If they are not installed, the user must install them manually. If they are not installed, pause executing this prompt and ask the user to install them using the Visual Studio NuGet Package Manager or Visual Studio package manager console.
6. Modify `web.config` to read app settings and connection strings from environment variables. Add configBuilders in conf
